analysis: Reviewed the head_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 3589-4069). Only documentation changed in the PR, with no code, key handling, protocol or attestation control touched. The visible text describes existing cluster behavior: tensor-parallel placement, link and share probe history, served speed records scoped by worker build, batch-invariant kernels, and Qwen/GLM tensor-parallel runtimes. It cites the same security properties as before: sealed AES-256-GCM all-sums, load agreements binding arithmetic and policy, owner-only ~/.darkbloom/cluster/*.json files, allowlisted rank environment (diagnostic switches such as DARKBLOOM_QWEN_TP_EXACT_VECTORS are not forwarded by an installed owner), tenant-partitioned prefix caches with an encrypted SSD tier (T-041 scope unchanged), and media digests bound into request digests. The documented changed ranges (Gemma pipeline lanes default, near lines 126-129, 3048, 3100, 4505-4538 and 4901+) are mostly outside the supplied excerpts. The excerpt for the Gemma serial-prefill pipeline default width and lanes is truncated, so I cannot verify its claims. The statement that GLM partials are sent as bfloat16 and added in float32 ('flagged for platform review') is a documented precision and numerical-equivalence note, not a confidentiality regression. Documented open items include the load-gate terms missing from the plan, and 'load' MTP depth policy not being lossless (default stays fixed). These are correctness and availability notes, not new attack surface. Remaining question: the patch for the Gemma 4 pipeline lane default (multi-lane installed default) could affect admission and resource limits (T-010, T-029) and should be checked in the code PR or in the unseen doc ranges. No security regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
